page: Amazon Web Services g6e.2xlarge is an accelerated computing instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The platform combines an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor operating at 3.4 GHz with dedicated hardware acceleration. The instance configuration provisions 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, 64 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, and a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps. Local high-speed storage is bundled in the form of a 450 GB NVMe SSD.

The primary accelerator is a single NVIDIA L40S GPU from the Ada Lovelace architecture, equipped with 45 GB of VRAM. Benchmark results reflect the specialization of this GPU setup, demonstrating top-tier (top 10%) performance in LLM inference across small and medium models. Specifically, it achieves 13,505.61 tokens per second on prompt processing for 135M models and 6,055.49 tokens per second for 7B models. Text generation rates reach 558.84 tokens per second on 135M models and 133.18 tokens per second on 7B models.

General-purpose computing and memory benchmarks demonstrate moderate performance. The AMD EPYC CPU delivers strong single-core stress-ng performance within the top 25% (2,992.9), while multi-core metrics like the Geekbench multi-core score (6,494.0) and PassMark CPU score (13,117.72) remain in the middle 50%. Large-block uncached memory read and write bandwidths measure at 39.1 GB/sec and 23.35 GB/sec respectively, placing in the lower quartile of tracked systems.

Hardware tradeoffs focus investment into graphical and neural processing rather than raw CPU concurrency or massive system memory bandwidth. The generous 45 GB VRAM allocation paired with bundled NVMe storage delivers high resource density for graphics-intensive tasks, rendering, and AI inference pipelines without requiring larger distributed GPU clusters.
description: Amazon Web Services g6e.2xlarge is an accelerated computing instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor and a single NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L40S GPU with 45 GB of VRAM. It features 8 vCPUs (4 physical cores) at 3.4 GHz, 64 GB of DDR4 memory, and a 450 GB NVMe SSD, complemented by a 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The system excels in machine learning inference, ranking in the top tier for small and medium model token processing, while delivering average multi-core CPU and memory bandwidth benchmarks. The hardware profile balances dedicated GPU acceleration with local high-speed storage, making the instance an efficient fit for AI model inference, graphics rendering, and video processing workloads.
